entries.subject: Refactor blockchain-k-plugin build (#1865)
entries.message:
Refactor blockchain-k-plugin build (#1865)

As we are starting to test the booster with more and more kevm proofs, we are hitting new corner cases with the LLVM dynamic library, which the booster uses for concrete execution. Specifically, we have come across the following error:

```
/tmp/hs-booster-proxy-bfeaddc9bbbd2ef1/.log: withFile: user error (dlopen: out/kompiled-llvm/interpreter.so: undefined symbol: _ZTVN8CryptoPP6SHA512E)
```

It turns out the linker is being too aggressive when pruning seemingly unused symbols from the dynamic library which results in the above error. The fix is to compile the offending library statically, producing a`.a` file and then instead of passing e.g. `-lcryptopp -L .../libcryptopp/lib`, we instead provide the static `.../libcryptopp/lib/libcryptopp.a` via `-ccopts` in `kevm-pyk`.

Since we now rely on static libraries for `libcryptopp`, `libff` and `libsecp256k1`, we build them from source, insterad of relying on the nix/system provided shared libraries.

entries.subject: Test lemmas for isStaticType and resulting encodeArgs values (#2376)
entries.message:
Test lemmas for isStaticType and resulting encodeArgs values (#2376)

* test lemmas for isStaticType and resulting encodeArgs values

In PR 2371, an `[owise]` attribute was added to `#isStaticType`.

The original reported issue was
[hs-backend-booster/issues/558](https://github.com/runtimeverification/hs-backend-booster/issues/558),
where a wrong rule was applied because of the missing `[owise]` (the
LLVM backend library evaluated the side condition to the wrong value).

This PR adds two lemmas to test the behaviour. On KEVM versions before
PR 2371 the tests fail when using `--use-booster` but succeed without it.

entries.message:
Add booster tests to CI (#1890)

The booster backend is now getting to the state where we can start testing against it for foundry proofs. This PR adds a CI run for the foundry tests with booster. Running with booster can be enabled for kevm foundry by first compiling with `kevm foundry-kompile ... --with-llvm-library` and then `kevm foundry-prove ... --use-booster`

entries.subject: kevm-pyk: thread step_timeout through run_prover (#2867)
entries.message:
kevm-pyk: thread step_timeout through run_prover (#2867)

Adds a `step_timeout: int | None = None` parameter to `run_prover` and
forwards it to the `APRProver` constructor, which enforces the per-step
wall-clock budget (interrupt + halve `execute_depth` + retry).

`step_timeout` is only honored on the sequential `advance_proof` path;
`parallel_advance_proof` does not wrap steps with the timeout budget. So
when `step_timeout` is set, `run_prover` runs sequentially regardless of
`force_sequential`, warning if `max_frontier_parallel > 1` that frontier
parallelism is being dropped.

Default `None` keeps the prior behavior (no per-step timeout, parallel
path unchanged).

Co-authored-by: Everett Hildenbrandt <everett.hildenbrandt@gmail.com>
